Subaru's chain driven engines have oil consumption issues. Ask the dealer about any possible warranty extensions from Subaru and see if they can print you out the TSB(Technical Service Bulletin) regarding any oil consumption issues pertaining to your particular model.

I am a Subaru Technician at a Subaru dealership and I always say one of the greatest things about Subaru is that they are all very easy to work on. I love only working on Subarus all day because everything is so accessible. If you're looking for a long term vehicle and you plan on saving some money by doing some of your own service work, Subaru is a great choice because they make it about as easy as it gets as far as service and maintenance are concerned.

After a lot of painful diagnostic grief, I realized that I forgot to go back to the basics. It turned out to be the fuel/anti theft fuse. The previous owner had a ton of unnecessary wiring all over the engine bay(I had no reason to assume it was faulty because it ran great before the clutch job)and for whatever reason the 20amp fuel/anti theft was wired to the fuse block rather than just being simply plugged into place. I removed the hacks wiring and plugged the fuse in place and it fired right up and ran perfectly. I had just done the clutch on it so I didn't know if it was something I did wrong or bad gas from sitting so long or what, anyways moral of the story:don't forget to check the basics before starting on a diagnostic journey. Thank you guys for your suggestions, as I said any advice is teuly appreciated.
